title: Prenatal p,p´-DDE exposure and neurodevelopment among children 3.5-5 years of age.
ehr_evidence: From 1 January 2001 through 30 June 2005, a prospective perinatal cohort study was assembled in Morelos, Mexico.
summary: In a prospective perinatal cohort study in Morelos, Mexico, prenatal maternal serum DDE exposure was negatively associated with child neurodevelopment (McCarthy Scales) scores at 42-60 months of age in 203 children.
key_findings: A doubling of serum DDE during the third trimester of pregnancy was associated with statistically significant reductions of –1.37, –0.88, –0.84, and –0.80 points in the general cognitive index, quantitative, verbal, and memory components respectively (β values).

Among the 84 children whose mothers had DDE measurements for all three trimesters, third-trimester DDE associations were significant and larger (β = –2.01, –2.06, –1.14, and –1.26 for GCI, quantitative, verbal, and memory).

The association with average DDE levels during pregnancy among children whose mothers had DDE measurements for all trimesters was significant for the quantitative component only (β = –1.78; 95% CI: –3.2, –0.4; p = 0.01).
No significant interactions with sex or breastfeeding were observed (interaction p-values > 0.10).

The association between third-trimester maternal serum DDE and the quantitative component varied by age, with a statistically significant interaction at 54 months versus 42 months, resulting in a weaker association at 42 months.
captured_features: Maternal serum DDE levels (ng/mL) by trimester
McCarthy Scales components (GCI, perceptual-performance, quantitative, verbal, memory, motor)
Maternal age, education, IQ, and marital status
Birth weight, gestational age, and type of birth
population: 203 children at 42-60 months of age (3.5-5 years) from a perinatal cohort in Morelos, Mexico; mothers recruited before pregnancy.
limitations: Loss to follow-up (attrition up to 42 months of about 30%).
Lack of information on postnatal DDE exposure.
Lack of validation of the McCarthy Scale in the Mexican population.
No information on postnatal lead exposure or infant nutrition.
